errors.text_span: Figure 5 is a grouped bar chart illustrating perplexity values for two methods (“Per-Output” and “Per-Layer”) across different sparsity rates. The horizontal axis contains the categories and is labeled “Sparsity Rate,” showing eight ordered tick labels from 10% through 80% in 10% increments. The vertical axis is the value axis labeled “Perplexity” and uses a logarithmic scale, with major tick marks labeled at approximately 10, 10², and 10³ (units not otherwise specified). Each sparsity category has two adjacent bars: a blue bar for “Per-Output” and an orange bar for “Per-Layer,” as indicated by the legend in the upper-left of the plot area. The bar heights (per the values shown on the page) are approximately: at 10% both methods are about 5.70; at 20% Per-Output ~5.81 and Per-Layer ~5.82; at 30% Per-Output ~5.99 and Per-Layer ~6.03; at 40% Per-Output ~6.38 and Per-Layer ~6.56; at 50% Per-Output ~7.17 and Per-Layer ~7.70; at 60% Per-Output ~9.35 and Per-Layer ~10.95; at 70% Per-Output ~20.46 and Per-Layer ~39.02; and at 80% Per-Output ~534.42 and Per-Layer ~886.10. The categories are presented in increasing sparsity order, the bars are not otherwise specially highlighted or annotated, and the chart includes faint horizontal gridlines aligned with the logarithmic tick marks.
errors.evidence: The description is excessively detailed, particularly in listing approximate numerical values for each sparsity rate, which is unnecessary for a high-level summary.
